nodes.summary: Let $G$ be a finite simple graph and let $p$ be an Eulerian trail in $G$, that is, a walk between any two vertices that uses every edge of $G$ exactly once. Then for every vertex $x$, the number of edges of $p$ that contain $x$, counted with multiplicity along $p$, equals the degree of $x$ in $G$.
nodes.title: Edges at a vertex of an Eulerian trail

nodes.summary: For every vertex $v$ of an edge-indexed multigraph $M$, the degree of $v$ equals the cardinality of the set of edges of $M$ whose endpoint pair contains $v$, where this cardinality is taken to be $0$ when the set is infinite.
nodes.title: Degree as the number of incident edges

nodes.summary: Let $M$ be an edge-indexed multigraph with finitely many vertices and finitely many edges. Then every vertex of $M$ has degree at most the maximum degree of $M$.
nodes.title: Degrees are bounded by the maximum degree

nodes.summary: The degree of a vertex $v$ in an edge-indexed multigraph $M$ is the number of edges of $M$ incident with $v$, that is, the cardinality of the set of edges whose endpoint pair contains $v$; it is defined to be $0$ when this set is infinite.
nodes.title: Degree in an edge-indexed multigraph

nodes.summary: Let $M$ and $N$ be edge-indexed multigraphs on the same vertex type. If the underlying simple graph of $M$ is connected, then the underlying simple graph of the disjoint sum of $M$ and $N$ is connected.
nodes.title: Adding edges preserves connectedness

nodes.summary: Let $M$ and $N$ be edge-indexed multigraphs on the same vertex type, each with finitely many edges. Then for every vertex $v$, the degree of $v$ in the disjoint sum of $M$ and $N$ equals the degree of $v$ in $M$ plus the degree of $v$ in $N$.
nodes.title: Degrees add under disjoint sums

nodes.summary: Let $M$ and $N$ be edge-indexed multigraphs on the same vertex type. Every edge $e$ of $M$, viewed as an edge of the disjoint sum of $M$ and $N$, has the same endpoints as in $M$.
nodes.title: Endpoints of edges from the first summand

nodes.summary: Let $M$ and $N$ be edge-indexed multigraphs on the same vertex type. Every edge $f$ of $N$, viewed as an edge of the disjoint sum of $M$ and $N$, has the same endpoints as in $N$.
nodes.title: Endpoints of edges from the second summand

nodes.summary: Given edge-indexed multigraphs $M$ and $N$ on the same vertex type $V$, with edge types $E$ and $F$, their disjoint sum is the edge-indexed multigraph on $V$ whose edge type is the disjoint union $E \sqcup F$, where an edge coming from $E$ has its endpoints in $M$ and an edge coming from $F$ has its endpoints in $N$.
nodes.title: Disjoint sum of edge-indexed multigraphs

nodes.summary: An edge-indexed multigraph with vertex type $V$ and edge type $E$ assigns to each edge $e \in E$ an unordered pair of endpoints in $V$, such that no edge has two equal endpoints. Distinct edges may have the same endpoints, so parallel edges are distinguished by their elements of $E$.
nodes.title: Edge-indexed multigraph

nodes.summary: Let $p$ be an indexed walk from $v$ to $w$ in an edge-indexed multigraph $M$, and let $e$ be an edge of $M$ with endpoints $u$ and $v$. The edge list of the walk from $u$ to $w$ that traverses $e$ and then follows $p$ is $e$ followed by the edge list of $p$.
nodes.title: Edge list of an extended indexed walk

nodes.summary: For every vertex $v$ of an edge-indexed multigraph, the edge list of the empty indexed walk at $v$ is the empty list.
nodes.title: The empty indexed walk has no edges

nodes.summary: For every indexed walk $p$ from $u$ to $v$ in an edge-indexed multigraph, the edge list of the walk in the underlying simple graph obtained from $p$ by forgetting edge identities is the list of the endpoint pairs of the edges of $p$, taken in the same order.
nodes.title: Edges of the forgetful walk

nodes.summary: The edge list of an indexed walk is the list of the edge identities it traverses, in order and with repetitions: the empty walk has the empty edge list, and the walk that traverses an edge $e$ and then follows an indexed walk $p$ has edge list $e$ followed by the edge list of $p$.
nodes.title: Edge list of an indexed walk

nodes.summary: In an edge-indexed multigraph with finitely many vertices and finitely many edges, the sum of the degrees of all vertices is even.
nodes.title: Handshake lemma for edge-indexed multigraphs

nodes.summary: Let $M$ be an edge-indexed multigraph with finitely many vertices and finitely many edges. Suppose that the subgraph of the underlying simple graph of $M$ induced on its non-isolated vertices is connected, and that every vertex of $M$ has even degree. Then there are a vertex $u$ and a closed indexed walk from $u$ to $u$ that is Eulerian, that is, it traverses every edge of $M$ exactly once.
nodes.title: Euler circuits in edge-indexed multigraphs whose non-isolated vertices are connected

nodes.summary: Let $M$ be an edge-indexed multigraph with finitely many vertices and finitely many edges. If the underlying simple graph of $M$ is connected and every vertex of $M$ has even degree, then there are a vertex $u$ and a closed indexed walk from $u$ to $u$ that is Eulerian, that is, it traverses every edge of $M$ exactly once.
nodes.title: Euler circuits in edge-indexed multigraphs

nodes.summary: Let $G$ be a finite simple graph in which every vertex has even degree, and suppose that the subgraph of $G$ induced on its non-isolated vertices is connected (in particular nonempty, so $G$ has at least one edge). Then $G$ has a closed Eulerian trail, that is, a closed walk that uses every edge of $G$ exactly once.
nodes.title: Euler circuits in simple graphs whose non-isolated vertices are connected

nodes.summary: Every finite connected simple graph in which every vertex has even degree has a closed Eulerian trail, that is, a closed walk that uses every edge of the graph exactly once.
nodes.title: Euler circuits in connected even graphs

nodes.summary: In an edge-indexed multigraph with finitely many edges, the degree of every vertex $v$ equals the number of edges incident with $v$.
nodes.title: Degree counts incident edges

nodes.summary: In an edge-indexed multigraph, a vertex $v$ is incident with an edge $e$ if and only if $v$ belongs to the unordered pair of endpoints of $e$.
nodes.title: Incidence is membership in the endpoint pair

nodes.summary: In an edge-indexed multigraph, a vertex $v$ is incident with an edge $e$ when $v$ belongs to the unordered pair of endpoints of $e$.
nodes.title: Incidence

nodes.summary: In an edge-indexed multigraph, an indexed walk is a walk that records which edge it traverses at each step. Indexed walks are defined inductively: for every vertex $v$ there is the empty indexed walk from $v$ to $v$, and if $e$ is an edge with endpoints $u$ and $v$ and $p$ is an indexed walk from $v$ to $w$, then traversing $e$ from $u$ to $v$ and then following $p$ is an indexed walk from $u$ to $w$.
nodes.title: Indexed walk

nodes.summary: Let $G$ be a simple graph and let $u$ and $v$ be non-isolated vertices of $G$, that is, vertices with at least one neighbour. If $v$ is reachable from $u$ in $G$, then $v$ is reachable from $u$ in the subgraph of $G$ induced on the set of non-isolated vertices.
nodes.title: Reachability among non-isolated vertices

nodes.summary: An indexed walk is Eulerian exactly when it is a trail whose edge list contains every edge identity of the multigraph.
nodes.title: Characterization of Eulerian indexed walks

nodes.summary: An indexed walk is Eulerian when it is a trail, that is, it uses no edge identity twice, and every edge identity of the multigraph occurs in its edge list.
nodes.title: Eulerian indexed walk

nodes.summary: An indexed walk is a trail exactly when its edge list has no duplicates.
nodes.title: Characterization of indexed trails

nodes.summary: An indexed walk $p$ in an edge-indexed multigraph is a trail when its edge list has no repeated entries, that is, $p$ traverses each edge of the multigraph at most once.
nodes.title: Indexed trail

nodes.summary: For an indexed walk $p$, the walk in the underlying simple graph obtained by forgetting edge identities has the same length as $p$, namely the number of entries in the edge list of $p$.
nodes.title: Forgetting edge identities preserves length

nodes.summary: Two edge identities $e_1$ and $e_2$ are adjacent in the line graph of an edge-indexed multigraph exactly when $e_1 \ne e_2$ and some vertex is incident with both of them.
nodes.title: Adjacency in the line graph of a multigraph

nodes.summary: The line graph of an edge-indexed multigraph is the simple graph whose vertices are the edge identities, two of them being adjacent when they are distinct and share an endpoint. In particular, parallel edges are adjacent.
nodes.title: Line graph of an edge-indexed multigraph

nodes.summary: For an edge-indexed multigraph with finitely many vertices and finitely many edge identities, the maximum degree is the largest degree of a vertex, and $0$ when there are no vertices.
nodes.title: Maximum degree of a multigraph

nodes.summary: If $e$ is an edge with endpoints $u$ and $v$ and $p$ is an indexed walk starting at $v$, then the support of the walk that traverses $e$ from $u$ to $v$ and then follows $p$ is $u$ followed by the support of $p$.
nodes.title: Support of a walk extended at the front

nodes.summary: The support of the empty indexed walk at a vertex $v$ is the one-element list $[v]$.
nodes.title: Support of the empty indexed walk

nodes.summary: Let $M$ be an edge-indexed multigraph and $p$ an indexed walk in $M$ from $u$ to $v$. The walk from $u$ to $v$ in the underlying simple graph of $M$ obtained from $p$ by forgetting edge identities visits the same vertices as $p$, in the same order: the two supports are equal as lists.
nodes.title: Forgetting edge identities preserves the vertex sequence

nodes.summary: The support of an indexed walk $p$ from $u$ to $v$ in an edge-indexed multigraph is the list of the vertices that $p$ visits, in order and with repetitions, including both endpoints: the empty walk at $w$ has support $[w]$, and a walk that starts at $u$ with an edge and continues with an indexed walk $q$ has support $u$ followed by the support of $q$.
nodes.title: Vertex list of an indexed walk

nodes.summary: Let $M$ be an edge-indexed multigraph. An indexed walk $p$ in $M$ from $u$ to $v$ yields a walk from $u$ to $v$ in the underlying simple graph of $M$ by forgetting edge identities: the empty indexed walk at $w$ goes to the empty walk at $w$, and an indexed walk that first traverses an edge $e$ with endpoints $\{u, x\}$ and then continues with an indexed walk $q$ goes to the walk that first steps from $u$ to $x$, an…
nodes.title: From an indexed walk to a walk in the underlying graph

nodes.summary: Let $M$ be an edge-indexed multigraph. Two vertices $u$ and $v$ are adjacent in the underlying simple graph of $M$ if and only if some edge $e$ of $M$ has endpoint pair $\{u, v\}$.
nodes.title: Adjacency in the underlying graph

nodes.summary: The underlying simple graph of an edge-indexed multigraph $M$ with vertex set $V$ is the simple graph on $V$ whose edges are the unordered pairs $\{u, v\}$ that are the endpoint pair of some edge of $M$; such pairs have $u \ne v$ because $M$ is loopless. It forgets edge multiplicities.
nodes.title: Underlying simple graph of an edge-indexed multigraph
Graph Theory

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
